gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false full-row diagonal lower bound caused by applying the weak-greedy guarantee only to the first batch member while later members use stale residual information.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof incorrectly extends the first-member weak-greedy lower bound to every member of an unfiltered batch, yielding a generally false diagonal estimate.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed diagonal bound is asserted for every batch member although only the first member satisfies the weak-greedy condition.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly states that only the first element has the weak-greedy property and that no corresponding guarantee exists for the remaining parallel elements.

component_coverage.gold_component: The stale-surrogate argument produces a false diagonal inequality and can fail even for linearly independent data.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 calls the displayed inequality unjustified and generally false and requires replacing or repairing the diagonal lower-bound property.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold entry bundles two independently diagnosable defects: the polynomial contradiction reuses an index-dependent C1 at an auxiliary index, and the exponential contradiction analogously mishandles c1. ISSUE-004 independently diagnoses the polynomial defect; ISSUE-005 independently diagnoses the exponential defect.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both bundled defects are failures to justify sharpened index-dependent rate constants when the contradiction compares a target index with an auxiliary index; the selected predictions cover the polynomial and exponential instances separately. No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: The polynomial and exponential cases use different constants and contradiction estimates, so their demonstrations are supplied by separate entries; no substantive gold concern is left unrecognised.
gold_decisions.combination_explanation: The gold issue contains two distinct defects: misuse of C1 across auxiliary and target indices in the polynomial proof, and misuse of c1 across those indices in the exponential proof. ISSUE-004 gives a self-contained diagnosis and repair for the former; ISSUE-005 gives a self-contained diagnosis and repair for the latter.

component_coverage.gold_component: The polynomial proof uses the same C1 at an auxiliary index even though C1(n,b) is index-dependent and monotonicity does not provide the required stronger estimate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly identifies the mismatch between C1(M,b) and the auxiliary-index terms and proposes fixing the constant or proving a genuinely index-dependent bound.

component_coverage.gold_component: The exponential proof compares c1 at the target index with bounds evaluated at an auxiliary index despite opposite monotonicity, so the displayed sharpened constants are unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 independently identifies the fixed-versus-index-dependent c1 error in the first-violation argument and proposes a fixed positive b-dependent replacement or a new proof.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the claimed unconditional batch rate-loss factor is obtained by replacing minimum-defined constants with selected first branches while ignoring the competing logarithmic branch; the equality is therefore not generally justified.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof treats the first branches of minimum-defined exponential constants as universally active and infers an unconditional (2/3)^alpha factor without the required branch condition.

component_coverage.gold_component: The actual constants are minima of a first branch and a logarithmic branch, but the proof simply asserts the first-branch values.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-006 explicitly states that the theorem constants are minima, that the asserted first-branch values do not follow, and that the logarithmic term is ignored.

component_coverage.gold_component: The unconditional exact rate-loss factor and n-to-2n/3 interpretation are unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-006 directly identifies the unsupported (2/3)^alpha factor and requires restating it using the actual constant or proving it under explicit conditions.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the Case 2 contradiction's false comparison: with q<L, one has Ls+q<2Ls rather than the asserted lower bound, so the ensuing monotonicity and exponent contradiction do not follow.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The Banach stretched-exponential Case 2 proof uses an inequality opposite to the one implied by its q-range, invalidating the subsequent comparison and contradiction.

component_coverage.gold_component: The Case 2 assumptions imply Ls+q<2Ls, contradicting the displayed comparison Ls+q>=2Ls.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-009 states the same q-range, derives the strict opposite inequality, and identifies the resulting invalid monotonicity direction.

component_coverage.gold_component: The false comparison leaves the displayed exponent contradiction unsupported and requires a corrected local rearrangement.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-009 requires fixing or reversing the Case 2 inequality and reproving the exponential estimate, which directly addresses the unsupported contradiction identified in the gold issue.
